The Concept of Consecration ♦ 5

'pratiṣṭhā' as the ritual of consecration with mantras
only and without any reference to the sculptor or the
icon that he fashions (Kriyā, 18, 7-8)

स्थापनं द्विविधं भवेत्।
स्थापनं च प्रतिष्ठा च स्थापनं शिल्पिसंयुतम्।
प्रतिष्ठा तद्विहीना स्यान्मन्त्रेणैव हि सा भवेत् ॥

More usual is the division of consecration into five
varieties, in which 'pratishthā' and 'sthāpanā' figure as
distinct ones. Varuṇa-śiva-paddhati, already quoted,
enumerates these varieties of pratishthā, which is a
ritualistic act of conjoining the pedestal with the linga:

पीठस्य विधिना योगः प्रतिष्ठा सा च पञ्चधा ।
प्रतिष्ठा स्थापनां स्थितस्थापनामास्थापनमुत्त्थापनमिति ।।

(1) Pratiṣhṭā: the linga which represents pure con-
sciousness is conjoined with the pedestal which sym-
bolizes primordial energy.

ज्ञानशक्तिस्वरूपे लिंगे क्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपस्य पीठस्य
विधिना योगः प्रतिष्ठा स्यात् ।

It is also called 'pīṭha-bandha', or fixing a seat.
Īśāna-śiva-guru-paddhati (Kriyā-pāda, paṭala 45) calls
it 'piṇḍikā-yoga' or providing a fixed pedestal for a
permanent shrine.

यत्र ब्रह्मशिलायां तल्लिंगमादौ निधाय तु।
क्रियते पिण्डिकायोगः तां प्रतिष्ठां प्रचक्षते ॥

This ritual is more suited to temples where liṅgas
are permanently located in the sanctum

6 ♦ The Āgama Encyclopaedia

(2) Sthāpanā: The variety of liṅga which is mobile
(like bāṇa-linga, or linga made in metal or precious
stone) is place on a pedestal during worship, without
any fixtures.

बाणलिंगादौ पीठे यथायोगनिवेशनं स्थापनं ।
धातुरत्नमयं लिंग बाणं वा लोहसम्भवं
स्थापितं पिण्डिकामध्ये स्थापनं तदुदाहृतम्उ

This ritual is relevant for worship at home; the liṅga,
small in size, is temporarily placed on a seat and
consecrated.

(3) Sthita-sthāpanā: the linga of the mobile variety
(made of metal of precious stone, or unsculpted by hand
like bāṇa-liṅga and svayambhū-liṅga) which has al-
ready a pedestal forming a natural part of the former
(viz. in one piece) is consecrated in this variety.

अभिन्नपीठस्य लिंगस्य संस्कारः स्थितस्थापनम्।

In the words of Īśāna-śiva-guru-deva-paddhati.(op.
cit)

रत्नहेमादि लिंगानामेका चेत् पिण्डिका तदा ।

Another text refers to the pedestal with an already
existent linga on it ('śiva-yute pīṭhe').

(4) Āsthāpanā: consecration of the pedestal first,
followed by the installation of the manifest liṅga on it
subsequently;

पूर्वं पीठमास्थाप्य तस्मिन् व्यक्तलिंगस्य
निवेशनमास्थापनम् ।।
चतुर्हस्तादिकं लिंगं युक्तलिंगमथापि वा।
summary: This section explains the concept of consecration in the Śaiva tradition, focusing on the installation of the linga. It first presents a two-fold distinction: 'sthāpanā' (स्थापनं), physical installation involving a sculptor, and 'pratiṣṭhā' (प्रतिष्ठा), a purely mantric ritual. It then details a more common five-fold classification of consecration from the Varuṇa-śiva-paddhati, defining the first four types: (1) Pratiṣṭhā, the permanent conjoining of a linga to its pedestal in a temple; (2) Sthāpanā, the temporary placing of a mobile linga for worship; (3) Sthita-sthāpanā, the consecration of a linga that is already integrated with its pedestal; and (4) Āsthāpanā, the consecration of the pedestal first, followed by the linga. The explanations are supported by Sanskrit quotations from authoritative texts like the Īśāna-śiva-guru-paddhati.
key_themes: Distinction between permanent and temporary worship
The role of mantras in ritual
The symbolism of the linga and pīṭha (pedestal)
main_arguments: The concept of consecration ('pratiṣṭhā') can be understood through different classifications, primarily a simple two-fold division and a more detailed five-fold one.
The distinction between 'sthāpanā' and 'pratiṣṭhā' initially hinges on the involvement of physical craftsmanship versus purely mantric rites.
A more nuanced classification identifies specific rituals for different contexts, such as the type of linga (permanent, mobile, self-manifest) and the location of worship (temple, home).
These classifications and definitions are rooted in and validated by authoritative Śaiva texts (paddhatis and āgamas).
methodology: The methodology is primarily textual and exegetical. The author defines and classifies the concept of consecration by citing, translating, and interpreting specific Sanskrit verses from primary religious and ritual treatises such as the 'Kriyā-pāda' of the 'Īśāna-śiva-guru-paddhati' and the 'Varuṇa-śiva-paddhati'. The approach is descriptive and analytical, aiming to present traditional categories of ritual practice as found in these source texts.
historiographical_context: The text operates within the scholarly field of Indology and specifically Śaiva Āgamic studies. It engages with the classical tradition by directly referencing and interpreting 'paddhatis' (ritual manuals) and 'Āgamas' (sectarian scriptures), which form the authoritative basis for Śaiva doctrine and practice. This work appears to be a modern scholarly encyclopedia or commentary that aims to systematically present and clarify traditional concepts for a contemporary audience, bridging classical textual knowledge with modern academic formats.
research_questions: What are the primary meanings and types of consecration ('pratiṣṭhā') within the Śaiva Āgamic tradition?
How do different authoritative texts classify the rituals of consecration?
What are the specific procedural and contextual differences between the various types of consecration, such as Pratiṣṭhā, Sthāpanā, Sthita-sthāpanā, and Āsthāpanā?
What is the scriptural basis for these distinctions and their respective applications in temple and home worship?
book_structure_overview: This section is structured as a systematic exposition of a key ritual concept. It begins with a broad, binary definition to introduce the topic. It then progresses to a more complex, numbered classification system (a five-fold division), which it elaborates upon point by point. Each point in the classification is defined, explained in its specific context, and substantiated with direct quotations from Sanskrit source texts, demonstrating a clear, hierarchical, and evidence-based explanatory structure.
